journey.title: Notice a session you did not start, and stop it
journey.purpose: The safety loop. A consumer the operator did not personally launch — a delivery ramp, an agent run, a scheduled flow — is driving a personal device. The operator must be able to notice it without looking for it, understand who holds it, and stop it immediately.

steps.intent: Notice, without having navigated anywhere in particular, that a device is under a held lease and see who holds it.
Identify which device is held, on which host and transport, and what it is currently permitted to do.
Read the running verb audit to understand what has already been done to the device.
Terminate the session immediately and confirm the audit record survives the termination.

claims.statement: The operator learns that a device is being driven without navigating to that device, and without having been the one who started the session.
claims.rationale: SECURITY.md's 'a session is left running unnoticed' threat. If noticing requires opening the right page, the mitigation depends on suspicion the operator has no reason to have.

claims.statement: Termination is available from the moment the session is noticed, without first navigating to the session page.
claims.rationale: The kill control lives in the lease bar rather than on the session screen so the distance between noticing and stopping is zero.

claims.statement: After the session is killed, the record of what was already done to the device remains readable.
claims.rationale: DVC-P0-009. Killing a session must not destroy the accountability record it produced, which is the only way to answer 'what did it do' afterwards.
